title: Mapping nonordinary experiences in a representative German sample: Phenomenology, prevalence and links to self-transcendence
content:
by Marc Wittmann, Julie Papastamatelou, Sepideh Ravahi, Liane Hofmann, Cecilia Bastos

This study investigated the prevalence, phenomenology, and potential transformative significance of nonordinary experiences in a representative German sample. Across cultures and historical periods, such experiences have been widely reported and often culturally valued. To assess these phenomena, the study employed the Inventory of Nonordinary Experiences (INOE; Taves et al., 2023), a phenomenologically grounded instrument that focuses on subjective experiential qualities rather than explanatory frameworks. The INOE was administered alongside two validated measures: the Questionnaire on the Phenomenology of Exceptional Experiences (PExE-II), which assesses frequency and types of anomalous experiences, and the Inventory of Secular/Spiritual Wakefulness (WAKE-16), which measures positive self-transformation. Data from 440 participants revealed that nonordinary experiences are widely distributed. Exceptionally strong emotional experiences (e.g., awe, love, loss) were most frequently reported, while explicitly anomalous phenomena (e.g., telepathy, sensed presences) were less common but still notable, with prevalence rates of 10–30%. Correlational analyses showed positive associations between INOE domains and PExE-II dimensions, suggesting that experiences more common in the population also tend to occur more frequently within individuals. In structural equation modelling, the INOE emerged as a significant positive predictor of the WAKE-16, indicating an association between nonordinary experiences and self-transcendent personality development. Overall, the findings support the perspective that nonordinary experiences constitute a widespread and meaningful aspect of human experience.
